bib.title: Chapter 2: Building a Multi-Agent System with MCP (Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Systems)
bib.venue: Packt (book chapter, O'Reilly web copy printed 12/26/25)

question: How do you build a small multi-agent system in which an Orchestrator, Researcher and Writer agent pass engineered context as structured messages, and how do you make it resilient and self-checking?
hypothesis: A team of specialist agents with structured message passing, retries, validation and a fact-check loop beats a single general LLM on complex multi-step tasks (asserted, not tested).
contributions: Orchestrator, Researcher and Writer agents exchanging a simplified MCP-style message dict
call_llm_robust retry wrapper, validate_mcp_message validator, Validator agent with a bounded revision loop

results.claim: The revision loop in final_orchestrator is capped at two writing attempts to prevent infinite cycles.
results.setup: Chapter's MAS_MCP_control.ipynb notebook; Writer drafts, Validator returns pass or fail plus feedback, feedback appended to the Writer's next prompt
results.note: The loop is `for i in range(max_revisions)`, so it is 2 writing attempts, i.e. one revision after the first draft.

results.claim: call_llm_robust retries a failed API call 3 times with a 5 second delay and returns None if all attempts fail.
results.setup: Default arguments of the chapter's retry wrapper around client.chat.completions.create
results.note: delay=5 seconds; no error-type filter, every Exception is retried.

results.claim: The chapter's 'MCP' message is a plain Python dict standing in for JSON-RPC, not the Model Context Protocol itself.
results.setup: Simplified protocol with keys protocol_version, sender, content, metadata; all agents run in one notebook
results.note: Text continues 'more than enough to illustrate this idea. It serves as our stand-in for the formal JSON-RPC object'.

results.claim: The validator only checks that the message is a dict with the four required keys, not their types or content semantics.
The pass/fail decision is a substring test, 'pass' in the lower-cased validator reply.
results.note: A fail explanation that contains the word 'pass' would be read as a pass.

limits: No experiment or measurement; the only output shown is one console run on one topic (Mediterranean diet).
Researcher reads a hard-coded simulated_database dict; topic is hard-coded in the first Orchestrator; RAG deferred to later chapters.
Agents run in one process; HTTP/STDIO transports and JSON-RPC are described but not implemented.
Model name differs between listings: call_llm uses gpt-5, call_llm_robust uses gpt-4.
Validator checks Writer against the Researcher's summary only, so errors in the summary pass through; no sampling or repeat runs.
practices: Define a structured message (sender, content, metadata) and use it for every agent hand-off (Defining the protocol).
Give each agent one narrow role through its system prompt (Building the agents).
Keep the Orchestrator free of specialist work; it only delegates and chains outputs (Architecting).
Wrap LLM calls in retries and return None on exhaustion so the Orchestrator decides (Building robust components).
Validate each message's structure before passing it on and stop the workflow on an invalid or empty message (Validating MCP messages).
Add a fact-checking Validator agent and cap the revision loop at 2 (final orchestrator).
Learn to build from scratch before adopting a framework such as autogen, CrewAI or LangGraph (Tools for building agent systems).

terms.definition: a system that can run multiple independent agents, each one specialized in a distinct task such as research, writing, or data analysis
a shared language: the rules for how agents pass tasks and information to one another, so every message is structured and reliable
the project manager that breaks the goal into steps, delegates, and passes one agent's result as context to the next (context chaining at system level)
Resilience: temporary API issues do not crash the system. Reliability: agents always exchange predictable, valid MCP messages
